name: Penny
description: Turn customer feedback into clear product priorities, roadmaps, and release updates.

capabilities.description: Publish Markdown release notes with separately approved local images, explicit public labels and product names, and YouTube/Vimeo videos loaded only on the reader’s choice. Filter the changelog by label and product; corrections retain the published snapshots.
Group roadmap items into dated internal release plans, link blockers and dependents, and flag slipped dependencies and affected approved public ETAs without changing public wording.

Save private or operator-shared comparisons of requests/features with native voters, accounts, evidence and importance, explicit manual RICE/value-over-effort/segment-demand/weighted-sum inputs and visible unknowns. Commercial, segment/date, custom-field, scorecard and delivery-estimate columns remain partial.

Organise requests into private products, components and features, attach roadmap work and retain links on moves. Feature demand counts distinct people, accounts, recorded account revenue and evidence.

Record a customer proxy vote from an inbox item, request card or private Zendesk sidebar, with private source/recorder attribution, one vote per customer, no identity verification or email consent, individual-voter CSV and portable custody. Zendesk proof uses its SDK/proxy edge fixtures; no live account installation is claimed.

Optional board-labelled voter importance, private per-request counts and source-stated proxy importance; saved Canny vote priorities retain reversible import receipts. Commercial values, prioritisation use and Productboard importance remain partial.

Reviewed saved Canny imports retain custom internal status names and can reconstruct a public status roadmap from selected public boards, with replay and conflict-safe undo. Imported requests remain held for native moderation; approval preserves their mapped status.

Preview and optionally notify eligible duplicate subscribers when merging; exclude existing canonical subscribers, defer private targets until publication, and preserve consent, opt-outs, quiet hours and durable delivery custody.
Operators explicitly approve a public month or quarter separately from private delivery windows; changing or removing it prepares a customer-safe update draft without sending it.
Flag overdue inbox work, unanswered comments, requests without a public response and stale public statuses; configure the ages, snooze evidence, and record one in-app owner reminder per age step.

Private source-cited cancellation investigation over selected native feedback and exact Orbit delegated evidence targets, with versioned interpretation, no-build comparison, pre-action commitment and bounded scheduled refresh. Requires explicitly configured enforcing transport and model/source secrets; live customer usefulness, hosted recurrence and all Stage 4–5 outcomes remain open.

Serve Penny's public product landing at `/`: the shipped capabilities only, links to the docs, the public board under /portal, the source and sign-in, a switchable footer credit, no operator data, no cookies and no third-party loads.
Render D1-backed approved feedback, roadmap and release reads in Start SSR and public Hono DTOs, with visible search, status filters and published-only duplicate suggestions.

Requester submission, votes, explicit follows, moderated comments and edits, withdrawal and activity including release-subscription controls, with separate provider email verification through Base. Decline closes new votes and requester comments, preserves discussion, and reverses to the previous status. Operators block and unblock requesters from the private directory; blocking hides their public contributions and excludes votes without deleting records. Existing appeals and host-signed identity are retained. Status changes record notification intent; notification delivery is a separate gate.
Serve public reads from explicit customer-safe projection DTOs without account, evidence, decision, or operator-only fields.

Maintained Base operator sessions authorize moderation, comment/edit review, status updates, merge/unmerge, boards, private tags, typed custom fields and separately approved attachments. Reviewed saved-Canny board mappings retain posting, comment and public-display policy. Private Hono and Start boundaries independently check Base admission.

Authenticated current-schema product archive over hosted HTTPS or loopback HTTP, with original request/evidence attachment bytes and explicit installation-authority exclusions. Guarded empty-store restore and supported-root erasure have an authenticated hosted API/CLI source path; hosted verification is source-only, local TLS. Restored pending requester and decision-review mail is held. Limits, operator holds and latest-journal continuity gaps remain explicit; universal data clauses and live hosted acceptance remain open.

Durable customer-safe public status/reply/approved-comment notifications, fixed first-event one-minute coalescing and owner-configured workspace quiet hours, drained by event-time Queue wakeups with a minute Cron backstop; selected provider acceptance, opt-outs and uncertain-send reconciliation are separately tested.

Saved classic CSV/API-response history, Ideas aggregate CSV and ideas-with-voters CSV exports use explicit mappings, private move-in receipts and reversible native custody; evidence is synthetic-only, real-export acceptance remains open, and no replacement is claimed.

Public operator documentation at /docs and /docs/<slug>: the repository Markdown that docs/site.json publishes, rendered to HTML at build time by a Vite plugin that fails the build on a broken internal link, under the product landing's header and footer; it reads no workspace record and an unknown page is a 404.

The owner chooses the workspace timezone during setup; Owners and Admins change it in settings, and can set requester quiet hours or turn them off. Existing installations confirm their timezone once. Decision reviews use the chosen timezone and operator email has no quiet hours.

Operators assign or unassign requests and evidence, set board defaults for capture and work their own request, evidence and requester-comment queue. Assignments remain private and portable without granting sign-in authority. Theme defaults remain unavailable.

nonGoals: Granular roles, permissions, and approval chains
A CRM, support inbox, survey, NPS, community chat, or general-purpose forum
Requester self-voting without verified identity; operator-recorded proxy attribution never grants identity
AI outside the bounded source-cited cancellation investigation in LEARN-001 through LEARN-006; no scoring, ranking or automatic merging
A combined priority score or automatic ranking of requests, bets, or roadmap items
Automated CRM/support breadth, review scraping and call ingestion beyond owner-selected Orbit evidence targets in LEARN-001
Imports from arbitrary feedback tools beyond the documented saved feedback CSV/API-response format
A script-tag feedback widget or in-app capture SDK beyond the embeddable portal in REQ-027
Portfolio capacity planning, Gantt charts, sprint management, and public delivery estimates

externals.why: Selected Base SendGrid or Resend transport sends operator links, requester verification and customer-safe requester notifications. Provider acceptance is not inbox proof. Resend receives each delivery key as its Idempotency-Key and suppresses a duplicate within 24 hours; SendGrid's delivery key is correlation only, so REL-007 provider suppression is unsatisfied for SendGrid. Ambiguous sends are held for operator reconciliation and never replayed.
data: recipient email address
single-use sign-in or verification link, or customer-safe notification content
delivery key for bounce and retry correlation

env.name: APP_ORIGIN
env.why: Canonical HTTPS origin for operator and requester links.

env.name: AUTH_SECRET
env.why: At least 32 characters; Base HMAC-domains operator session, link and rate-limit tokens.

env.name: OPERATOR_EMAIL
env.why: Deployment owner email, added to the server-configured operator allowlist without removing existing operators.

env.name: SETUP_TOKEN
env.why: Independent secret of at least 32 characters, required once to bootstrap an empty Base operator store.

env.name: MAIL_PROVIDER
env.why: Select sendgrid, resend or rer (Managed), or later for public reading without email; MAIL_API_KEY is required for every provider.

env.name: MAIL_FROM
env.why: Sender verified with the selected mail provider.

env.name: MAIL_API_KEY
env.why: API key for the selected MAIL_PROVIDER (SendGrid, Resend, or the RER-issued Managed relay credential); required unless MAIL_PROVIDER=later.

env.name: PORTAL_IDENTITY_SECRET
env.why: Optional host-signed requester identity secret; verified-email identity remains available without it.

env.name: SENDGRID_EVENT_PUBLIC_KEY
env.why: Required to accept SendGrid signed Event Webhook callbacks; canonical base64 P-256 public verification key.

env.name: RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET
env.why: Required to accept Resend signed Event Webhook callbacks; Svix whsec signing secret.

env.name: PENNY_LEARNING
env.why: Optional JSON for scoped cancellation learning: an orbit section (HTTPS origin, delegated token, pinned installation, audience principals, read cost) and a model section (model, API key, token prices, output bound). It is used only with the PENNY_LEARNING_EGRESS enforcing RPC service binding; without both, Learning reports unconfigured and refuses work.

env.name: PENNY_DISCORD
env.why: Optional Discord applicationId, Ed25519 publicKey, botToken and gatewaySecret JSON. Installation custody only. Requires PENNY_DISCORD_EGRESS and an owner-run Gateway relay; disabled when absent.

deploy.notes: Operator credentials use maintained Base operator-auth; requester email is sent through the selected Base SendGrid or Resend transport. GET /auth/confirm previews a link without consuming it; same-origin POST confirms it. Private Hono and Start functions authenticate independently. Production has no local outbox switch. 0009 revokes prior synthetic credentials. Test-only predecessor fixtures are separate from production Base tests. Setup packages clean production artifacts; deploy targets the rer-seedproof-penny workers.dev prefix via Base. Hosted/provider proof remains separate from local verification. Required requester mail and minute-Cron notification drain are declared in OPERATIONS.json. Provider credentials, verified sender, hosted Cron execution and inbox delivery need independent proof. The public feedback board's canonical address is /portal/feedback, and /portal redirects there (9 October 2026). /docs and everything under /docs/ are public build-time documentation pages (DOCS-001) that read no workspace record and set no cookie; an unknown docs page is a 404.

limits.provenance: All values are estimates for backend design and must be replaced by load-test results before the first release. Latency that defines a feature lives in its contract clause, not here.

operatingCost.basis: Workers Free is the default Cloudflare plan; Workers Paid starts at USD 5 per account-month. Requester notification delivery consumes event-time JOBS Queue wakeups and uses the minute Cron as a backstop; both send through the selected provider with the same durable claims. For the future release-delivery limit, a normal Queue message at or below 64 KB is at least three operations (write, read, delete): 3,334 successful deliveries consume at least 10,002 operations and exceed Workers Free's 10,000 Queue operations per account per UTC day. A maximum 50,000-recipient release needs at least 150,000 Queue operations before retries, dead-letter handling, or messages above 64 KB, so it genuinely requires Workers Paid. Workers Free D1 includes 5 million rows read/day, 100,000 rows written/day, and 5 GB total storage; reaching a Free D1 limit makes D1 return errors until the UTC reset or an upgrade. R2 Standard includes 10 GB-month storage, 1 million Class A and 10 million Class B operations/month; using R2 requires a billing-enabled Cloudflare account even while usage remains within those included allowances. The R2 free tier does not apply to Infrequent Access storage, which also has retrieval fees and a 30-day minimum storage duration. Cron Triggers are included; this port does not currently use Durable Objects. R2 and Workers do not charge Internet egress under the documented plans. Transactional email remains a separate provider and message-volume cost.

monthlyUsd.cloudflare: Workers Free by default; Workers Paid starts at 5, then Queue, D1, R2, and Worker usage above included allowances are usage-dependent
